title: On Wondering whether the letter had gone astray
subtitle: 情感心理 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）
meta: 主题语境：情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）　|　核心词汇：wonder　|　正文 364 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 wonder 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1959 the counsellor ① wondered whether the letter had gone astray on the same day, and every listener in the garden said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three evenings on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the counsellor ② wonders whether the letter had gone astray before dawn without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ wonder whether the letter had gone astray at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ wondered whether the letter had gone astray before — a line in the journal for June 1953 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Wondering whether the letter had gone astray on the same day, the counsellor said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the letter at the far bench, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ wonder at the silence of the whole street before dawn, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Wonder at the silence of the whole street at once and never mention it again.

By 1966 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the journal, and a new listener from the next garden ⑧ wonders at the silence of the whole street on the same day every evening without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the bench, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ wondered whether the letter had gone astray again when nobody else would.

⑩ To wonder whether the letter had gone astray, my mother said in 1971, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the garden remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the garden forgets, somebody wonders whether the letter had gone astray before dawn again and somebody must wonder whether the letter had gone astray on the same day all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 想知道（一般过去式 wondered whether the letter had gone astray：1959 年谈心人头一回这样做，当天就）
B. v. 想知道（一般现在 wonders whether the letter had gone astray：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 想知道（不定式 to wonder whether the letter had gone astray：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 想知道（过去完成时 had wondered whether the letter had gone astray：1953 年六月的心记上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 想知道（动名词 wondering whether the letter had gone astray 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 诧异（wonder at the silence of the whole street：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去诧异对整条街的沉默感到诧异）
G. v. 诧异（wonder at the silence of the whole street：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 想知道（后段两处：新来的倾听者照例 wonders at the silence of the whole street，而母亲又一次 wondered whether the letter had gone astray）

answers.why: wonder 意为“想知道”，1959 年谈心人当天就想知道不知那封信是不是寄丢了，那是小园里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 wondered。
wonder 意为“想知道”，自那以后谈心人天没亮就把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 wonders。
wonder 意为“想知道”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯想知道不知那封信是不是寄丢了”，此处为不定式 to wonder whether the letter had gone astray。
wonder 意为“想知道”，心记里 六月 那行字说明早在 1966 年之前就有人想知道过，故用过去完成时 had wondered。
wonder 意为“想知道”，谈心人说“想知道不知那封信是不是寄丢了这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 wondering whether the letter had gone astray 作主语。
wonder 意为“诧异”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去诧异对整条街的沉默感到诧异”，should ever 之后用原形 wonder at the silence of the whole street。
wonder 意为“诧异”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻诧异对整条街的沉默感到诧异（wonder at the silence of the whole street at once），以后再也不要提起。
wonder 意为“想知道”，新来的倾听者每个黄昏都照例诧异对整条街的沉默感到诧异，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 wonders。
wonder 意为“想知道”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次当天就想知道不知那封信是不是寄丢了，用一般过去式 wondered 叙述。
wonder 意为“想知道”，结尾那句是母亲 1971 年的话：要想知道不知那封信是不是寄丢了，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和小园记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 wonder 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1959 the counsellor wondered whether the letter had gone astray on the same day, and nobody in the garden forgot it.
Even now the counsellor wonders whether the letter had gone astray before dawn whenever the garden asks.
Wondering whether the letter had gone astray on the same day, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever wonder at the silence of the whole street before dawn, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new listener from the next garden wonders at the silence of the whole street on the same day every evening, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother wondered whether the letter had gone astray again, and the garden remembered that half.
